findings.reason: if the fallback is only reached when the selection found no record at all, a "delivered but unpromoted at the current head" probe reads the same nothing the selection read and can never fire; the repair would add a guard on a path the incident did not take and leave the real one open, which is exactly the node's whole deliverable.
findings.text: the ancestor fallback runs only under `if stored is None and described:` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:852`), and `stored_review_for_run` reaches `select_review_for_head`, whose store docstring says a committed record at another head falls through to the staging store "for one at that head before the tree reports the absence" (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:566-570`); the run's own `review-records/` holds a delivered record at `76a7b7bfae` and another at `a1305995c4`, so on the delivered-review path the selection should already have returned a record and the fallback should not have been reached. The plan names the cause as a missing question about a delivered review without showing which revision the run stood at when the three disposes ran, or that the record for that revision was invisible to the selection — and its second anecdote (one review record keyed at `e1d54ab0a0`, the filed record at `d2626bdd97`) points at head-keying, not at a missing probe

findings.reason: without the sentence the node's gate log can land in a session scratchpad or carry no readable exit status, which is the failure the plan's other 25 sections were written to prevent, and adding one line costs the author nothing.
findings.text: s26's done-when names no log location, no first-line content and no `EXIT=` last line, while s25 (§155) and the plan's other sections each say "Every log is under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command, and ends in `EXIT=`"; promotion reads the gate's exit status from that log, so a worker here may write its gate anywhere

findings.reason: the case is unwinnable for a test author who dates the fixture before the audit threshold, and the plan's only mention of the audit is an incidental "on a record written after the" in a docstring the node never reads, so the node would burn its budget discovering a precondition the plan should state.
findings.text: s25's fourth case asserts the advice "names the other as unclassified" for a finding carrying neither severity nor prefix, but `unmarked_findings` returns `[]` when `_record_predates_unmarked_audit` is true, which it is for any record stamped before `UNMARKED_SEVERITY_AUDIT_STARTED_AT` (`reckon/crew/repair.py:182-196`); a fixture stamped with a fixed earlier date therefore cannot satisfy the case, and the plan does not say the record must be stamped after that constant

findings.reason: the section cannot be retitled or split by its coordinator while the heading under-describes two of its three deliverables, and a reviewer closing the node on the severity work alone would leave the merged-head guard unmeasured.
findings.text: the heading promises a round that "reads each finding's severity and its disposition", but the third deliverable is "No round starts for a run whose reviewed head is already reachable from the integration branch", which is neither: it is a third, unrelated condition on when a round starts, and the section's own disposed-finding bullet is context that `blocking_findings` and `tests/test_a_disposed_finding_ends_its_repair_round.py` already enforce
